document_title: Struck. And Still Printed. Alaska's $500 Cap
post_copy:
Alaska's statute, as codified, still prints a $500 cap on giving to a candidate.
The Ninth Circuit struck it on July 30, 2021, and nobody re-set the book.

So what is the limit? Unlimited, per the Alaska Public Offices Commission's table, for Alaskans and non-residents alike. One person put $100,000 into the governor's race.

Does the August 18 ballot fix it? Measure 1 asks whether to write $2,000 back in. Even a yes takes effect ninety days after certification, which lands after the November general.

Inside, the statute beside the agency table, four donation totals at one scale, and both sides of Measure 1.

This page runs on Anthropic's Claude. Six of its employees gave $372,000, not the company.

Alaskans set this cap themselves in 2006 with 73 percent. Measure 1's sponsors are buying no ads. Does it clear the August ballot anyway?

#AlaskaCampaignFinance #BallotMeasure1 #AKleg

Every deadline this deck tracks, August 3 and August 11 and August 18 included, stays current on the docket at https://alaskaaihq.com

If you have read these filings yourself, or you have context this deck missed, add it below. Corrections get made in public.

Sourcing note

The $500 statute figure comes from the published codification and from the Ninth Circuit's own text, because the state's bill server was unreachable on every route tried. No APOC filing was read directly for this deck, so every dollar figure here is press reported off filings rather than pulled from the filing itself. The next round of state disclosures is due August 11, and it will move these numbers.

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time, and take the earliest of those slots you can get. This deck has a short shelf life. Early voting opens August 3, the next filing lands August 11, and the primary is August 18.
Paste the first comment within 60 seconds of posting, unedited and as plain text, so every raw URL survives the paste and stays readable.
Stay on the post for the first 60 to 90 minutes and reply substantively to every comment. The ballot question is live and people will bring filings you have not seen.
If a commenter says Anthropic donated, correct it plainly and immediately. Six employees gave personally, the company gave nothing, and Anthropic has issued no statement of any kind.
At 48 hours, note saves and comments against the last five decks and log the delta in the ledger.
